assessment: Here's the secret to your fetch quests: this deck's tutors are couriers, not genies. Worldly Tutor, Congregation at Dawn, Enlightened Tutor, and Forerunner of the Empire all put the wish on TOP of your library — it arrives next draw, not now. So you schedule wishes, you don't spend them. Every wish serves one of two clocks. Clock one: Gishath's mean cast turn is 7.97 in the goldfish, so anything that shaves that number — Sol Ring, Urza's Incubator — is a wish for tempo. Clock two: the reveal. When Gishath connects, every Dinosaur in the flipped cards hits the battlefield free (stack 001 turns one 7-damage swing into five bodies and three draws), so a wish stacked on top before combat is a free-roll with your name on it. And don't sleep on the ping web: stack 005 proves one Forerunner ping converts a Dinosaur ETB into removal, ramp, and draw. Several wishes below exist purely to feed it. Top-deck the right card and you're never drawing blanks — you're drawing appointments.

targets.scenario: Turn 2, end of an opponent's turn. Your hand has lands and mid-cost Dinosaurs but no acceleration. The table is developing quietly.
targets.why: This is your default wish. One green at end of turn, draw Selvala, cast her turn 3. Her tap makes X mana where X is your greatest power — any 5-power Dinosaur turns her into a rocket. The strategic frame is blunt: Selvala online drags the Gishath pivot forward two-plus turns off the naked 7.97 mean. Buy the clock first, spend it on dinosaurs after.

targets.scenario: You're behind. Two opponents have wide boards of Elves, Zombies, and tokens. You hold eight lands and this tutor. Your next untap is your rebuild turn.
targets.why: The behind fetch nobody expects from a beatdown deck. Top it, draw it, cast it from your hand — and because you cast it from hand, it destroys every non-Dinosaur creature on the battlefield. Your board is Dinosaurs. Theirs isn't. That's a one-sided apocalypse stapled to a 7/7, and it's why the wish beats fetching a blocker.

targets.scenario: Closing time. You have five bodies on board — the goldfish says that's your turn-10 board on rails — and you need one more haymaker to end it.
targets.why: Ghalta costs {10}{G}{G} minus the total power of your creatures. With a real board she's two green mana for a 12/12 trampler. The tutor is instant speed: wish at end of turn, draw, deploy, swing. When you're already ahead, the cheapest 12 power in the deck is the fastest door out of the game.

targets.scenario: Pantlaza's discover trigger is on the stack off a toughness-5 Dinosaur. You hold one green mana and this tutor. The top of your library is unknown.
targets.why: The wish nobody sees coming. Worldly Tutor is an instant — cast it in RESPONSE to the discover trigger. It resolves first, Regisaur Alpha goes on top, and discover 5 exiles it and casts it free: a 4/4, a 3/3 token, and haste for the team. Stack 001 already taught you that Pantlaza rewards the pilot who controls trigger timing. This is the graduate course.

tutors.notes: Every Worldly wish is public — you reveal the card. The table sees Wakening Sun's Avatar coming a full turn out, so cast this one at the last legal moment.

targets.scenario: Gishath is on board and unblocked. Before damage — or the night before the swing — you cast Congregation with the reveal coming.
targets.why: The signature play. Stack three Dinosaurs on top and Gishath's 7-damage reveal free-rolls all of them (stack 001 is the proof of concept). Polyraptor headlines, with Trapjaw Tyrant and Ripjaw Raptor behind it — that's the entire enrage web from stack 005 arriving in one combat step. An 8-drop, a 5-drop, and a 4-drop for three mana and one connection. That's the best exchange rate this deck offers.

targets.scenario: A wrath just cost you the board. You have eight mana available next turn and the table smells blood.
targets.why: Top it, draw it, hand-cast it: every non-Dinosaur creature dies and you keep a 7/7. Stack Vaultborn Tyrant second — you'll draw it the turn after, and it draws you a card and gains 3 life on entry. Congregation says 'up to three,' and here you want the known rebuild more than live draws. You're not recovering. You're counterattacking on a schedule.

targets.scenario: Descendants' Path is on the battlefield. It's an opponent's end step and your upkeep is next.
targets.why: The quiet one. Path reveals your top card at upkeep and casts it free if it shares a type with your board. Congregation guarantees the reveal — and because Path CASTS Zacama, its untap-all-lands trigger fires. A free 9/9 and all your mana back, at upkeep, before you've even drawn. Three mana at instant speed has never bought more.

tutors.notes: You choose the order of the three. Card one is this turn's promise; cards two and three are your next two draws — never stack a third card you wouldn't be happy topdecking in a fire.

targets.scenario: Turn 1, on the play, one white source. Your hand is lands and five-drops.
targets.why: The tempo wish. The goldfish gives you 2.14 mean mana on turn 2 — Sol Ring turn 2 makes it four and cascades from there. Gishath's mean cast turn is 7.97; every early mana point is a direct attack on that number. One mana at end of turn one is the cheapest turn you'll ever buy.

targets.scenario: Mid-game, hand full of Dinosaurs, commander in the zone. You need the whole hand to get cheaper, not one card to get better.
targets.why: Your default wish. Name Dinosaur and every Dinosaur spell costs {2} less — the deck carries 34 threat bodies, so the Incubator discounts most of your library, including Gishath down to six mana. The goldfish tracks 'cost reducer drawn' at mean turn 3.0 for a reason: this is the card that turns a turn-8 commander into a turn-6 one.

targets.scenario: You're behind on cards after trading through an early skirmish. Board has one 4-power body, hand is thinning.
targets.why: The grind wish. It replaces itself on entry with a 4-power creature out, then pays every time a big body lands — stack 001 shows a single Gishath reveal converting into THREE Uprising draws. Trample on the team is the bonus that turns chump blocks into damage. When the game goes long, this is the engine that keeps your hand full of dinosaurs.

targets.scenario: The blue player has held up counter-mana for three straight turns and already ate your Regisaur Alpha. Your hand is stocked; your spells keep dying on the stack.
targets.why: The flank attack. Once the Portal resolves naming Dinosaur, {3} and a tap PUTS any Dinosaur from your hand onto the battlefield — no cast, no stack, nothing to counter, at instant speed on their end step. Their counterspells are now paper. Watch them start tapping out again, right into your combat step.

targets.scenario: Default: Forerunner enters on turn 4 with a developing board and no immediate pressure on you.
targets.why: Top the raptor, draw it, and the moment it lands you own the web's crown jewel. Stack 003 verifies the line: Forerunner pings on each Dinosaur ETB, each surviving Polyraptor copies itself, and every single sweep is optional — you stop the chain whenever the math says stop, tokens in hand, no drawback. A bounded burst you control completely. That's not a gamble; that's a dial.

targets.scenario: Descendants' Path is on the battlefield and your upkeep is coming.
targets.why: Forerunner guarantees the Path reveal is a Dinosaur — and Path casting Zacama for free triggers her untap-all-lands clause, since a Path cast is still a cast. A 9/9 with built-in removal, life, and enchantment hate, at upkeep, mana refunded. The Forerunner fetch is the aim; the Path is the trigger.

targets.scenario: You're behind: an opponent's Voltron creature is one swing from eliminating you and your removal spells are spent.
targets.why: The defensive wish. Draw it, land it, and now every Forerunner ping exiles a creature an opponent controls — stack 005 shows one ping converting into exactly that exile. Every Dinosaur you cast afterward is a removal spell with legs. You're not stabilizing. You're installing a turret.

targets.scenario: Gishath swings unblocked next turn and Forerunner just entered. The reveal is coming.
targets.why: Guarantee the first card Gishath flips. Vaultborn hits the battlefield free off the reveal (stack 001 mechanics), gains you 3, draws you a card, and its 6 power triggers every big-body payoff you have out. Even when it eventually dies, it leaves a copy behind. The reveal was already good — this makes it certain.

tutors.notes: Forerunner is a Human Soldier, not a Dinosaur. Gishath's reveal never puts it into play free and Roar of the Fifth People can't find it — when you want the web's hub, Worldly Tutor and Congregation at Dawn are the only couriers that deliver it.

tutors.card: Huatli, Poet of Unity // Roar of the Fifth People

targets.scenario: Huatli enters on turn 3 and your hand is short a white source.
targets.why: White is your thinnest colour — 12 land sources against 14 green and 13 red — and the deck's steepest pip demand is Wakening Sun's Avatar at {W}{W}{W}. Huatli's entry search puts the basic in your HAND, so it's a guaranteed land drop. Default to Plains unless your hand says otherwise; the deck-facts pip math says it will rarely say otherwise.

targets.scenario: You're a turn or two from casting Gishath and your board can produce {G} and {W} but red is nowhere.
targets.why: Gishath demands {R}{G}{W} exactly, and Trumpeting Carnosaur and Etali both want double red behind it. When the commander is the plan, fetch the pip the plan is missing. A dead-on-colours turn 8 beats a stranded turn 7 every time.

targets.scenario: Wayward Swordtooth is on the battlefield and you've already played your land for the turn.
targets.why: The sleeper synergy: the search puts the basic in hand, and Swordtooth's extra land drop plays it the SAME turn. That's Huatli quietly ramping you a full land ahead — 38 of your cards carry green pips, so the Forest is never wasted. Small edge, every game, compounding.

targets.scenario: Roar of the Fifth People sits on chapter III at your upkeep. The blue player has counter-mana up every turn and your last two threats died on the stack.
targets.why: The Roar search takes ANY Dinosaur straight to your hand — so take the one they cannot touch. Carnage Tyrant can't be countered and has hexproof. Cast it into their open mana and smile. One upkeep later, chapter IV gives it double strike and trample. Fourteen uncounterable damage says the control game is over.

targets.scenario: Chapter III triggers with Forerunner of the Empire on the battlefield and chapter II already turning your team into mana.
targets.why: The closing wish. Chapter II's creature-mana pays the {6}{G}{G}, and Polyraptor entering hands Forerunner the dial from stack 003 — optional pings, self-copying raptors, stop whenever the math peaks. Then chapter IV lands: double strike and trample on every copy. You built the army and the kill turn on the same card. That's poetry, and Huatli knows it.

tutors.notes: The real quest is the transformation. Pay {3}{R/W}{R/W} at sorcery speed and the Saga starts the countdown: chapter I makes two 3/3s, chapter II turns your whole team into mana, chapter III is the wish above, and chapter IV is double strike and trample on every Dinosaur you control. Time the flip so chapter IV lands on your kill turn. Read the table, count three upkeeps, and roar.

gaps: No instant or sorcery tutor exists in the 99. The one-sided Blasphemous Act line — Temple Altisaur plus Wrathful Raptors turning a 13-damage wrath into 16 at an opponent's face (stack 004) — can never be assembled on demand. You draw Blasphemous Act or you don't. When you do, protect it like the finisher it is.

Every creature wish is a delivery, not an arrival: Worldly Tutor, Congregation at Dawn, and Forerunner of the Empire all put the card on TOP, one draw away. Against a table holding sweeper mana, the wish can die in transit — Ripjaw Raptor and Curious Altisaur draws are your couriers, and instant-speed tutoring at an end step shortens the exposure to zero turns.

Forerunner of the Empire — the ping web's hub — is a Human Soldier. The Gishath reveal never free-rolls it and no Dinosaur-only search finds it. Only Worldly Tutor and Congregation at Dawn can locate the engine piece the whole stack 005 web hangs on. Budget one of those wishes accordingly when the web is your game plan.
